findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when there is no destination calendar
findings.body: The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar (defaulting to []) and then dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is undefined, null, or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws a TypeError, aborting EventManager.create for bookings that have no destination calendar configured instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous evt.destinationCalendar?.integration check did.

findings.title: Google update/delete lose the destination-calendar fallback
findings.body: In updateEvent (lines 254-256) and deleteEvent (lines 315-317), when externalCalendarId is falsy the fallback searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals that same falsy externalCalendarId, which can never match. Previously it fell back to the event's destination calendar. Updates therefore call Google with calendarId undefined, and deletes fall back to 'primary' instead of the calendar the event was created on, so collective/other-host events can fail to update or be deleted from the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services still always use the first destination calendar
findings.body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination calendar/credential, but Office365 (lines 73-77), Lark (CalendarService.ts lines 128-129), and the CalDAV base service (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts line 156) ignore the credentialId/externalId for the current iteration and always select destinationCalendar[0]. For a collective booking, the second host's credential is therefore used to create an event on the organizer's calendar id: it will typically 404/fail, or duplicate the event on the wrong calendar, and the other host's own calendar never receives the event. Only the Google service was taught to find the destination matching credentialId.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the collective handling then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). When it is null the optional-chained push is a no-op, so destination calendars collected from collective team members (users.slice(1)) are discarded even though those hosts do have calendars, and their calendar events are never created.

findings.title: Video booking references lose their credentialId on creation
findings.body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId to result.credentialId only for calendar results and to undefined for everything else. Previously video results kept result.credentialId. Booking references for video meetings are consequently persisted without a credentialId, and later flows that look up the specific video credential from the reference (e.g. cancellation deleting the meeting only when reference.credentialId is present) can no longer find/delete the meeting, leaving orphaned video meetings.

findings.title: updateLocation creates booking references with no calendar/credential identifiers
findings.body: updateLocation now builds references from result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's returned EventResult never populates either field (its return object contains only appName/type/success/uid/updatedEvent/originalEvent/calError/calWarnings). editLocation.handler persists these referencesToCreate, so after a location change the booking's calendar references have externalCalendarId and credentialId undefined, breaking subsequent updates/cancellations that need them to address the correct host calendar.

findings.title: Unrelated change breaks organization slug assignment
findings.body: This PR changes slug handling from 'set slug when team billing is disabled, set requestedSlug when it is enabled' to 'set both slug and requestedSlug only when billing is enabled, and neither otherwise'. On non-billing/self-hosted instances organizations are now created with no slug at all, and on billing instances the slug is assigned immediately, bypassing the requested-slug verification flow. This is unrelated to destination calendars and can break org routing/creation.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: When newBookingId is supplied, the cleanup uses booking.references.find(...) to locate a single old calendar reference and deletes only that event. Bookings created by this PR can have one reference per collective host, so the old events on all other hosts' calendars are left behind as orphaned/stale events after a reschedule merge.

findings.title: Confirming a collective booking only creates the organizer's calendar event
findings.body: The confirmation path rebuilds the CalendarEvent with only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar as a one-element array; the other collective hosts' destination calendars stored at booking time are not reconstructed (the Booking row itself only persists the first one). Since calendar events for requiresConfirmation bookings are created on confirmation via handleConfirmation/EventManager.create, the non-organizer hosts will not receive calendar events for confirmed collective bookings, which is the scenario this PR sets out to fix. The same single-calendar reconstruction exists in the Stripe/PayPal payment-success handlers.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape for destinationCalendar changes and is inconsistent
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changes from a DestinationCalendar object/null to an array, and CalendarEvent objects are spread directly into webhook payloads. External consumers (webhooks/Zapier) that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId will break. The value is also now inconsistent for 'no destination': handleNewBooking emits null while confirm/cancel/payment flows emit [], so consumers cannot rely on a single shape; only one of the three webhook e2e expectations was updated to match.
